title: US P-EBT disbursements increased sugary-item spending among eligible households
source_unit: US SNAP-eligible households with school-aged children, P-EBT disbursement timing, weekly sugary-item spending, overall food spending, and placebo households
geography: United States; state-level P-EBT disbursement timing

observations.period: Working paper issued October 2026; pandemic P-EBT disbursement period

denominator.unit: SNAP-eligible households with school-aged children in the NielsenIQ Consumer Panel; exact panel count not disclosed in the NBER abstract

sugary_item_spending.unit: percent increase in weekly spending on sugary items after P-EBT disbursement

overall_food_spending.unit: sugary-item spending increased more than overall food spending for the eligible group

allocation_share.unit: eligible households allocated a disproportionately large share of P-EBT-driven purchases toward sugary items relative to their pre-period baseline

placebo_households.unit: no changes were detected among households unlikely to have received P-EBT benefits or in placebo disbursement years

observations.method: A stacked difference-in-differences design uses state-level variation in P-EBT disbursement timing and NielsenIQ Consumer Panel purchase data.
observations.uncertainty: The NBER abstract does not disclose panel counts, effect intervals, exact sugary-item definition, spending levels, or all parallel-trend and composition assumptions. The finding measures purchases, not consumption, nutrition, health, household food security, or long-run behavior.
observations.subgroup: SNAP-eligible households with school-aged children during the pandemic P-EBT program; unlikely recipients and placebo years provide comparison boundaries.
observations.counterinterpretation: Purchases may reflect stocking, substitution, household sharing, prices, retailer timing, or measurement of sugary items rather than direct consumption; eligibility and receipt may be imperfectly observed, and pandemic conditions may limit generalization.

related_sources.claim: SNAP sugary-drink restrictions reduce excluded-drink purchases while increasing perceived stigma and producing substitution toward still-eligible drinks.
Medicaid nursing-home financing can expand program volume toward lower-quality providers and reduce survival in the studied setting.
USDA food-security measures provide a household food-access boundary that purchase data alone cannot establish.

boundary: This record adds a direct purchase-response layer to the US safety-net program. It does not establish sugary-item consumption, nutrition, health, food security, household welfare, or a universal response to cash-like food assistance.
